summary: Implement a local library borrowing application per the architecture documents: Node.js22 + Express gateway serving a plain HTML/CSS/JS browser UI and REST API, backed by PostgreSQL16. Two business modules (catalog and loans) live inside one deployable gateway service. Borrowing/returning use transactions with row locks on a single client; schema bootstraps idempotently without overwriting user books. npm test runs meaningful unit tests against a test-only in-memory adapter (no live PostgreSQL); real database behavior is exercised by the protected runtime HTTP acceptance via Docker Compose.

tasks.description: Project scaffold: package.json (Node22 runtime, pinned deps, build/test/start scripts), .gitignore, .env.example.

contracts.description: Pinned npm dependencies for express and pg; real build/check script 'npm run build'

tasks.description: PostgreSQL schema with idempotent bootstrap (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS) plus optional seed; never overwrites user-created books on repeat startup.

contracts.description: Idempotent schema; seed only when empty so repeated startup preserves user books

tasks.description: Data access layer with repository interfaces and two implementations: a real PostgreSQL repository and a test-only in-memory repository sharing the same repository API (dependency injection).

contracts.description: Repository API (createBook, listBooks, getBook, createLoan, listLoans, getLoan, returnLoan, borrow) shared by PG and in-memory adapters

tasks.description: Catalog business module: create book with positive copies, list books with available copies, get single book (404 on missing).

contracts.description: createBook validates title non-empty string and copies positive integer; listBooks returns books with availableCopies

tasks.description: Loans business module: borrow with transaction + row lock, at most one active loan per (bookId,userId), idempotent return restoring stock exactly once.

contracts.description: borrow(bookId,userId) locks book row, validates stock and duplicate active loan, decrements available, returns active loan; 409 on exhausted or duplicate, never negative stock (origin=assumption derived from borrow sequence)
returnLoan is idempotent: returns loan status 'returned' and increments stock only on first transition

tasks.description: Express app wiring routes to catalog/loans modules and health endpoint, with a factory taking a repository (dependency injection) so tests inject the in-memory adapter.

contracts.description: Endpoint mapping per REST interface; status codes 201/200/400/404/409/200 idempotent return

tasks.description: Gateway entrypoint: connect PostgreSQL, run idempotent schema bootstrap, serve UI and API, expose /health; .env-driven connection.

contracts.description: Listen on 3000, serve static UI at /, /health returns 200, bootstrap schema on startup

tasks.description: Browser UI: plain HTML/CSS/JavaScript page listing books, entering reader ID, borrowing and returning with clear success/error feedback; no authentication.

contracts.description: Frontend lists books and available copies, borrow via explicit reader ID, return a loan, clear feedback

tasks.description: OpenAPI spec documenting all REST endpoints and responses.

Unit tests using in-memory repository covering FR1-FR5, NFR1 (single-copy concurrency), idempotent return, validation errors; schema bootstrap idempotency (NFR2) via a fake pool; no live PostgreSQL required for npm test.

contracts.description: Tests run without a live database using in-memory adapter; assert exactly one success among eight simultaneous single-copy borrowers

tasks.description: Deployment: Dockerfile (gateway Node22), docker-compose.yml (gateway on 3000, postgres on 5432), healthcheck wiring.

contracts.description: Compose services gateway (container 3000) and postgres (container 5432); gateway serves UI and /health (origin=supplement)

tasks.description: Documentation: README and architecture-decisions (assumptions, deferred scope, concurrency reasoning).

contracts.description: README documents run/test/build, distinguishes fake-infrastructure tests from real runtime acceptance

assumptions: Reader IDs are caller-provided strings without authentication (stated in both original and supplement); no OAuth is introduced.
Book IDs and loan IDs are generated by the application (SERIAL/auto-increment) since the interface only names id/status fields; labeled origin=assumption.
availableCopies is stored as an integer column and mutated under row lock inside transactions; no separate inventory table is required by the design.
The test suite uses an in-memory repository for unit/API testing so npm test runs without PostgreSQL; runtime acceptance exercises the real PostgreSQL path via Compose.
Loan status values are 'active' and 'returned' (stated in REST interface and loan state diagram).
The gateway container port is 3000 and postgres 5432; Compose maps them to host ports, and tests must not assume the host port equals the container port.
conflicts: Original design names PostgreSQL16; supplement references PostgreSQL without a version. Resolved: pin postgres:16 per the original NFR2.
Original says 'separate business modules' inside one gateway; supplement allows them to share one deployable service. Resolved: two modules (catalog, loans) in one gateway process, matching both.
Original does not mandate Compose port mapping details; supplement fixes gateway=3000/postgres=5432. Supplement is authoritative for the independent acceptance contract.
